runs.why: setup shell scripts + requirements split — the #164 anchor
runs.summary: Adds one-command setup scripts for macOS and Windows plus reorganized backend requirements files. The scripts are reasonably thorough but contain some duplicated pytest/httpx entries across requirements files, unvalidated remote script execution, and fragile assumptions (e.g., PATH refresh, exact string matching for versions) that could silently fail on some systems.

comments.comment: pytest==8.3.3 and httpx==0.27.2 remain in requirements.txt (production dependencies) while pytest is also declared in requirements-dev.txt. Test-only dependencies like pytest should not be in the base requirements.txt; this causes duplication and installs test tooling in production environments.
comments.suggestion: Remove pytest==8.3.3 from requirements.txt since it's already declared in requirements-dev.txt as a dev-only dependency.

comments.comment: Piping curl output directly to bash without verifying checksum/signature is a common security anti-pattern for installer scripts, even though it's a widely-used pattern for Homebrew/nvm installers.
comments.suggestion: Consider documenting this risk in the script or README, and optionally pin to a specific commit/tag for the install script URL.

comments.comment: sed -i '' assumes GNU/BSD sed syntax specific to macOS; if JWT_SECRET_KEY line doesn't exist in .env.example or has different formatting, this silently does nothing and the script proceeds with an unset/placeholder secret without any validation.
comments.suggestion: Verify the sed replacement succeeded (e.g., grep for the generated secret afterward) and error out if not.

comments.comment: python --version output goes to stderr on some Python versions, and 'findstr "3.11"' would also match versions like 3.110 or paths containing '3.11' elsewhere; the check is fragile. Also PATH refresh via refreshenv depends on Chocolatey being installed, which isn't guaranteed here.
comments.suggestion: Use a more robust version check (e.g., parse major.minor explicitly) and don't rely on refreshenv unless Chocolatey is confirmed present.

comments.comment: The JWT_SECRET_KEY replacement embeds a Python one-liner with escaped quotes inside a batch file; if backend\.env doesn't already contain a 'JWT_SECRET_KEY=' line (e.g., .env.example format changes), this silently produces no replacement and no error is raised.
comments.suggestion: Add a check after generation to confirm the JWT_SECRET_KEY value was actually replaced, erroring out otherwise.

runs.summary: Straightforward, well-justified refactor merging two parallel registries into one keyed by extension, reducing risk of drift between grammar and language-name maps. Added tests directly verify registry integrity. No functional issues found.

runs.why: backend Python with real logic + a migration (METRIC-2)
runs.summary: Well-tested feature adding end-to-end §8.1 timing metrics (queued_at, total_ms) threaded from webhook receipt through Celery to the Review model. The implementation is careful about timezone-awareness, naive-vs-aware validation, clock skew clamping, and backward compatibility across rolling deploys. A couple of minor robustness/logging concerns remain.

comments.comment: _wall_clock_ms silently clamps negative durations to 0 with no logging/metric emitted for the skew case, making significant clock disagreement between API and worker hosts invisible to operators. Consider at least a debug-level log when the raw delta is negative, since this signals infra drift, not just a display concern.

_parse_received_at swallows all parse/type errors and returns None silently, matching the 'never fail a review over a metric' intent, but there's no logging to distinguish a malformed timestamp from a legitimate None (e.g. manual trigger). Over time this makes diagnosing systematic clock/serialization issues harder.
comments.suggestion: Log at debug/info level when value is non-None but fails to parse, so persistent parsing failures are diagnosable without affecting review success.

runs.summary: Adds a RequireAuth route guard, a UserMenu disclosure component, return-to stash/clear helpers, and test infrastructure updates. Overall well-reasoned and thoroughly tested. A few minor concerns: potential race/ordering nuance in stashReturnTo being called unconditionally on every anonymous render (including the logout redirect window before clearReturnTo runs), and the styleGuideRoute/shellRoute duplication of errorElement wrapping worth double-checking for dev vs prod route generation. No blocking issues found.

comments.comment: stashReturnTo is called as a side effect during render (not in an effect), which happens on every render where status is 'anonymous', including re-renders unrelated to a new navigation attempt (e.g., React strict-mode double-render, or parent re-renders during the loading->anonymous transition). This is called out and handled at the logout call site via clearReturnTo's ordering, but the underlying pattern of performing a side effect (writing to sessionStorage) directly in the render body is fragile and could cause subtle races if RequireAuth re-renders multiple times before Navigate actually takes effect.
comments.suggestion: Consider moving the stash into a useEffect keyed on location, or accept the current design but document that render-phase side effects here are intentional and safe because sessionStorage writes are idempotent per identical path.

comments.comment: onLogout awaits logout() then calls clearReturnTo(), relying on the assumption that RequireAuth's stash-on-anonymous-render happens synchronously during the re-render triggered by the status change from logout(). If React batches/updates the AuthContext consumer asynchronously (e.g. via concurrent rendering or a microtask boundary), clearReturnTo could run before RequireAuth's render, leaving the stash in place. Tests do cover this via StatefulAuth, which is good, but worth flagging as a subtle timing dependency between two separate modules that isn't enforced by any contract.

runs.why: docs only — should produce approve with zero comments
runs.summary: This PR adds a static, self-contained HTML architecture report page (docs/report.src.html generator source and the built frontend/public/report.html) plus a new favicon and .gitignore entries for local build tooling. The content is documentation/marketing copy with inline CSS/JS; no application logic is touched. Main concerns are around the generated-file duplication workflow, an inline unbounded IntersectionObserver/script pattern, and a factual inconsistency in the copy about metric definitions.

comments.comment: build-report.py and deploy-preview.sh are the only tooling that produces frontend/public/report.html from docs/report.src.html, but they are gitignored and thus not committed anywhere in this repo. Future contributors editing docs/report.src.html have no way to regenerate frontend/public/report.html without reconstructing this tooling from scratch.

The note titled 'A contradiction found in our own specification' documents (in the shipped copy) a real inconsistency between the 'approval rate > 70%' and 'false positive rate < 20%' targets, concluding it needs to be 'resolved and documented rather than quietly implemented wrong.' Shipping this acknowledged-but-unresolved contradiction as permanent user-facing documentation is odd — it reads as an internal note that leaked into the final copy rather than a decision. Consider resolving the metric definitions before publishing, or clearly framing this as a known open issue with a tracking link.

This ~2000-line file is described in its own header comment as GENERATED FILE — do not edit, produced by a generator script that is intentionally excluded from the repo (see .gitignore additions for build-report.py, deploy-preview.sh). This means the actual source of truth (the generator) is not reviewable or reproducible by other contributors, and the only way to verify the build output matches docs/report.src.html is manual diffing. Consider committing the generator script (even if simple) so the build is reproducible in CI, or at least documenting the exact transformation steps (e.g. what replaces __NEON_SRC__/__ARGON_SRC__) in the repo.

The inline theme-detection script duplicates the pattern used in frontend/index.html (reading `liffy-theme` from localStorage and toggling `.dark`/`.light` classes on `<html>`), but is copy-pasted here rather than shared. Since this is a static, non-bundled page that may be acceptable, but if index.html's key name or class semantics ever change, this copy will silently drift out of sync.
